reason: The core twist of the story—that Uranus's lopsided magnetic field was a 'solar wind fluke' discovered in 2024—is only found in one site (Wikipedia [S2]). Other key 'weird' details like the 2020 plasmoid discovery and the planet being the 'coldest' in the solar system also fail the two-site requirement, leaving the sources unable to support the specific surprising narrative requested.
story: In 1977, NASA launched Voyager 2 on a 'Grand Tour' of the outer solar system, a mission made possible by a rare planetary alignment that occurs only once every 176 years. By 1986, the probe reached Uranus, becoming the only spacecraft ever to visit the ice giant. It discovered a world of unexpected complexity, including ten previously unknown moons, a dark ring system, and a magnetic field that was bizarrely offset from the planet's geometric center. Using gravity assists to slingshot from planet to planet, Voyager 2 eventually reached Neptune before beginning its final journey into the void. Today, the spacecraft is the second-farthest human-made object from the Sun, having crossed into interstellar space in 2018. It continues to transmit data back to Earth via the Deep Space Network in Australia, carrying a Golden Record of human civilization into the eternal darkness of the Milky Way.
angle: For 40 years, our only close-up data on Uranus suggested it was a magnetic misfit—but we might have caught it on a one-in-twenty 'bad hair day' caused by the solar wind.

claims.claim: Voyager 2 was launched on August 20, 1977, from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited the ice giant planet Uranus.
The probe arrived at Uranus on January 24, 1986, passing within approximately 81,500 km of its cloud tops.
Voyager 2 was launched 16 days before its twin, Voyager 1.
Voyager 1 traveled on a faster, shorter trajectory to reach Jupiter and Saturn before Voyager 2.
The mission took advantage of a rare planetary alignment occurring once every 176 years to visit all four giant planets.
The use of gravity assists cut the flight time to Neptune from 30 years down to 12.
Voyager 2 discovered 10 previously unknown moons during its encounter with the Uranian system.
The spacecraft confirmed that Uranus possesses a system of rings.
Uranus's magnetic field is significantly offset from the planet's geometric center.
The rotation period of Uranus is approximately 17.24 hours.
Voyager 2 officially entered interstellar space on November 5, 2018.
Communications with Voyager 2 are managed by the Canberra station of the NASA Deep Space Network.
Voyager 2 is one of five spacecraft to achieve the solar escape velocity required to leave the solar system.

disputed: The 2024 analysis claiming the magnetosphere's shape was a solar wind fluke is only mentioned in Wikipedia; a script should attribute this to a 'recent re-analysis of old data.'
Sources vary between 10 and 11 new moons discovered at Uranus; a script should say 'at least ten.'
The launch gap between the twin probes is cited as 16 days by Wikipedia/PDS but as 'within 15 days' by Scientific American; attribute to specific dates (Aug 20 and Sep 5).
